articles.titleKo: 한지집 전시는 전통 한국 제지술을 기념합니다
articles.summaryKo: 홍보: 올해 파리에서 열리는 메종&오베 가구 박람회 중 전시회가 천 년 된 한국 제지 기법인 한지의 지속적인 중요성을 보여줄 예정입니다. 파리-노르 빌르팽트 전시장 내에 위치한 이 전시는 한국의 전통 수제 종이인 한지의 현대적 잠재적 활용을 보여주는 것을 목표로 합니다. 한지는 주로 내부 나무껍질로 만들어집니다
bodyKo: 홍보: 올해 파리에서 열리는 메종앤오브제 가구 박람회에서 열리는 전시회는 한지라는 천 년 된 한국 제지 기술의 지속적인 중요성을 보여줄 예정입니다.
파리-노르 빌르팽트 전시 센터 내에 위치한 이 전시는 한국의 전통 수제 종이인 한지의 현대적 잠재적 활용법을 보여주는 것을 목표로 합니다.
한지는 한국에서 유래한 전통 종이의 한 형태입니다. 위: 한국 회사 Fides International Co 한지의 한지 시트는 주로 뽕나무의 내부 나무껍질 섬유를 채집하고 가공하여 전통적인 기법을 사용합니다.
수확된 긴 섬유는 밀도 높은 그물망을 형성하여 내구성 있고 통기성이 좋으며 습도 조절이 가능한 종이를 만들어내며, 독특한 질감과 희미한 반투명성을 지닙니다.
스크린은 한지의 전통적인 응용 중 하나입니다. 한국 브랜드 큐레이티드 컬럼스의 스크린 전통적으로 종이는 글씨와 페인트로 쓰이고, 창문 장식과 바닥재로도 사용됩니다.
한지는 이제 문화유산 보존부터 가구 제작, 조명 디자인, 라이프스타일 제품 제작에 이르기까지 더 넓은 용도로 활용되고 있습니다.
한지 하우스는 7개의 한지 중심 디자인 브랜드와 제조업체의 작품을 선보입니다. 한국 브랜드 툴프레스의 부채 이 응용들은 2026년 메종&오브제트 기간 동안 한지 하우스라는 이름의 전시회에서 시연되었으며, 한국 공예 및 디자인 재단(KCDF)이 큐레이팅한 한지 전문 7개 한국 기업의 활동을 통해 선보입니다.
한국공예디자인재단(KCDF)은 "한지하우스는 방문객들이 한지의 부드러운 빛 확산과 공기 흐름에 대한 반응성을 경험할 수 있는 쇼룸으로 기획되었습니다."라고 밝혔습니다.
"전시는 한지를 단순한 종이가 아니라 공간을 형성하고 정의할 수 있는 현대적 재료로 제시한다."
이 종이는 염색, 글씨, 그리고 채색이 가능합니다. 한국 한지박 소재 연구소 및 한국 산업 디자인 스튜디오 SWNA의 한지 시트는 금속과 돌 등 단단한 재료와 결합된 한지의 적응력을 탐구하는 네 가지 가구 및 조명 작품을 선보일 예정입니다.
이 작품들은 현대 가구와 공간 디자인 맥락에서 한지의 잠재력을 보여주기 위해 제작되었으며, 조명 역할도 겸하는 칸막이와 우아한 곡선으로 이루어진 캐비닛과 조명 작품이 포함된다.
SWNA는 SWNA와 함께 한국 기업인 한지박 재료 연구소, 피데스 인터내셔널, 툴프레스, 소미당, 마르케지 G, 큐레이티드 컬럼스, 풀밧과 함께 네 점의 가구 및 조명 작품을 선보일 예정입니다.
이들은 전통적인 수제 한지와 보존지부터 공예품, 문구류, 실내 물건, 향수 제품, 조명에 이르기까지 다양합니다.
한자 제작 기술은 약 천 년 전의 역사를 가지고 있습니다. 소미당 한지가의 제품은 유네스코가 "한자 및 관련 문화 제작과 관련된 전통 지식과 기술"을 인류문화유산 대표 목록에 등재할지 여부를 결정하기 전에 진행되었습니다.
이 결정은 올해 말에 내려질 것으로 예상됩니다.
한지의 반투명성은 조명 디자인에 강력한 선택지입니다. 한국 디자인 브랜드 풀밧의 램프 "한지는 수세기 동안의 장인정신과 전통 제지 기술을 구현하면서도 오늘날 디자인 산업이 추구하는 지속 가능성과 다재다능함을 제공합니다,"라고 KCDF 회장 김경배가 말했습니다.
"한불 외교 140주년을 맞아 유네스코 결정이 다가오는 이 의미 있는 해에, 한지의 아름다움과 현대적 잠재력을 세계와 나누고, 한국 전통 문화에 뿌리를 둔 기업들이 국제적으로 확장할 수 있는 더 큰 기회를 만들고자 합니다."
현대 기업들은 한지의 전통을 이어가고 있습니다. 마르카주 G의 박스 한국공예디자인재단(KCDF)은 대한민국 문화체육관광부 산하의 공공기관입니다.
이 작품은 9월 10일부터 14일까지 메종&오베 2026의 일환으로 파리-노르 빌팽트 전시센터 7홀의 시그니처 갤러리에서 전시될 예정입니다.
자세한 정보는 메종&오브제 웹사이트를 방문해 주세요.
Maison&Objet 2026은 9월 10일부터 14일까지 프랑스 파리 노르 빌팽트 박람회장에서 열립니다. 전 세계 건축 및 디자인 행사에 대해 Dezeen 이벤트 가이드를 참고하세요.
이 기사는 Dezeen이 KCDF를 위해 파트너십의 일환으로 작성했습니다. Dezeen 파트너십 콘텐츠에 대해 더 알아보려면 여기를 클릭하세요.
한지하우스 전시가 전통 한국 제지를 기념하다 이 글은 Dezeen에 처음 게재되었습니다.

articles.titleOriginal: Lung Fibrosis Drug Lowers Biological Age Estimates
articles.summaryOriginal: Six different aging clocks detected younger blood protein profiles in patients taking the experimental lung-fibrosis drug rentosertib. This suggests possible […]

bodyOriginal.text: Six different aging clocks detected younger blood protein profiles in patients taking the experimental lung-fibrosis drug rentosertib. This suggests possible anti-aging effects, but separating those from the narrower benefits of treating fibrosis remains a challenge [1].

The AI-developed drug Many drugs developed for particular diseases act on aging-related biological processes. That creates an opportunity: a clinical trial could investigate both whether a drug treats its intended disease and whether it has broader effects on aging. Ordinary clinical measurements cannot establish those broader effects, but we now have biological age clocks that closely track chronological age or predict mortality risk [2]. These clocks have been used in numerous trials as proxies to estimate the intervention’s effect on aging.

In a new study published in Nature Biotechnology , the researchers analyzed blood samples from a Phase 2a trial whose results were published last year [3]. That 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested rentosertib, an inhibitor of the kinase TNIK, which has been implicated in several aging-related processes [4].

Rentosertib was developed by the longevity biotech company Insilico, using a proprietary AI-based drug discovery platform, to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a progressive disease in which excessive scar tissue compromises lung function. IPF is age-related, with a mean age of onset around 65 years, and aging processes such as cellular senescence and inflammation are heavily involved.
The new analysis included 42 of the trial’s 71 participants. Alongside placebo, the trial tested three regimens: 30 milligrams once daily, 30 milligrams twice daily, and 60 milligrams once daily.

Lower biological age readings The researchers used six different proteomic clocks, which analyze protein levels in blood. The proteomic clocks’ appeal is partly interpretability: researchers can identify which proteins affect the readings and connect them to known biological processes more directly than is often possible with methylation-based clocks. The clocks were developed by different teams, using data from UK Biobank, including one clock developed by Insilico itself. Four of the clocks were trained on chronological age, and two on mortality.

All six clocks detected lower predicted biological ages in patients taking rentosertib, although not at every dose or visit. After four weeks, the four chronological age-based clocks rated patients taking 60 milligrams once daily (the single-dose regimen) roughly three years younger, on average, than at the start of treatment. These changes were statistically significant compared with placebo. However, the two clocks trained to predict mortality risk did not show a significant change at that dose at week four.

Patients taking 30 milligrams twice daily (the split-dose regimen) showed the most consistent decreases across both types of clocks. The largest reductions in predicted biological age appeared by week four, with little additional change over the remaining eight weeks.

These results essentially mean that patients’ blood protein profiles became more similar to those associated with younger people. They do not, however, establish that the treated patients regained years of youth or would live longer.

Is there a broad anti-aging effect? Looking beyond the clock readings, the researchers found that treatment changed the levels of 326 blood proteins, including proteins involved in fibrosis, metabolism, and cellular stress responses. Most changes in the two higher-dose groups persisted throughout the trial or appeared later in treatment, suggesting that the drug continued affecting patients’ biology even after predicted ages plateaued.

The researchers then examined which proteins contributed most to the younger age estimates. A fibrosis-associated protein, LTBP2, stood out as a major contributor. It was used by all six clocks, which raises the question of whether their agreement mainly reflects the drug’s effect on fibrosis, rather than broader slowing of aging.

To explore whether the lower age estimates reflected more than improvement in fibrosis, the researchers compared changes in predicted age with changes in lung function. The two did not closely track each other. This suggests that improved lung function alone might not explain the clock changes, although lung function does not capture every aspect of IPF.

The team then compared the treatment-induced protein changes with differences between younger and older participants in UK Biobank. With the split dose, proteins associated with aging tended to move in the opposite direction: those found at higher levels in older people tended to decrease, and vice versa. This pattern was not statistically significant with the single daily dose.

Finally, the researchers examined proteins associated with cellular senescence. These proteins tended to increase in the placebo group but decrease with treatment, suggesting that rentosertib might reduce senescence-associated activity, although the researchers did not directly measure senescent cells in tissues.

These findings strengthen the case for investigating rentosertib as a potential geroprotector. However, because fibrosis, metabolism, and senescence are closely connected, they still cannot definitively establish whether the drug affects aging beyond its benefits for IPF.

“This study illustrates how biomarkers of aging can be incorporated into conventional clinical trials,” Vadim Gladyshev, a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School and a coauthor of the study, told Lifespan News. “If validated more broadly, such approaches could allow us to learn not only whether a treatment affects a particular disease, but also whether it influences some aspects of aging biology.”

articles.titleKo: 폐섬유증 약물, 생물학적 나이 추정치 감소
articles.summaryKo: 6개의 서로 다른 노화 시계가 실험적인 폐섬유증 약물 렌토서티브를 복용하는 환자들에서 젊은 혈액 단백질 프로필을 발견했습니다. 이는 가능성을 시사합니다 [...]
bodyKo: 6개의 서로 다른 노화 시계가 실험적 폐섬유증 치료제 렌토서티브를 복용하는 환자에서 젊은 혈액 단백질 프로필을 검출했습니다. 이는 노화 방지 효과 가능성을 시사하지만, 섬유증 치료의 좁은 이점과 구분하는 것은 여전히 도전 과제입니다 [1].

AI가 개발한 약물 특정 질병을 위해 개발된 많은 약물들이 노화 관련 생물학적 과정에 작용합니다. 이로 인해 기회가 생깁니다: 임상시험은 약물이 의도한 질병을 치료하는지와 노화에 더 넓은 영향을 미치는지 모두 조사할 수 있습니다. 일반적인 임상 측정으로는 이러한 광범위한 효과를 확인할 수 없지만, 현재는 나이와 밀접하게 일치하거나 사망 위험을 예측하는 생물학적 나이 시계가 있습니다 [2]. 이 시계들은 중재가 노화에 미치는 영향을 추정하는 대리 지표로 수많은 임상시험에서 사용되었습니다.
Nature Biotechnology에 발표된 새로운 연구에서, 연구진은 작년에 발표된 2a상 임상시험의 혈액 샘플을 분석했습니다[3]. 그 12주간의 무작위 이중 맹검 플라세보 대조 시험은 여러 노화 관련 과정과 관련된 것으로 알려진 키나제 TNIK의 억제제인 렌토서티브를 시험했습니다[4].
렌토서티브는 롱제비티 생명공학 기업인 인실리코(Insilico)가 독자적인 AI 기반 신약 개발 플랫폼을 사용하여 폐 기능을 저해하는 진행성 질환인 특발성 폐섬유증(IPF)을 치료하기 위해 개발했습니다. IPF는 연령과 관련이 있으며, 평균 발병 연령은 약 65세이며, 세포 노화세포와 염증과 같은 노화 과정이 크게 관여합니다.
새로운 분석에는 71명의 참가자 중 42명이 포함되었습니다. 플라세보와 함께 이 임상시험은 30밀리그램을 하루 1회, 30밀리그램을 하루 2회, 60밀리그램을 하루 1회 복용하는 세 가지 요법을 시험했습니다.

낮은 생물학적 나이 측정값 연구진은 혈액 내 단백질 수치를 분석하는 여섯 가지 단백질체 시계를 사용했습니다. 단백질체 시계의 매력은 부분적으로 해석 가능성에 있습니다: 연구자들은 어떤 단백질이 측정에 영향을 미치는지 파악하고, 메틸화 기반 시계보다 더 직접적으로 알려진 생물학적 과정과 연결할 수 있습니다. 이 시계들은 UK 바이오뱅크의 데이터를 활용해 여러 팀에 의해 개발되었으며, 그 중 하나는 인실리코가 직접 개발한 시계입니다. 네 개의 시계는 연대기적 연령, 두 개의 사망률에 대해 훈련되었습니다.

여섯 개 시계 모두 렌토서티브를 복용한 환자에서 예측 생물학적 나이가 낮아졌으나, 모든 용량이나 방문에서 나온 것은 아니었습니다. 4주 후, 네 개의 연대기적 연령 기반 시계는 하루 한 번(단일 투여 요법) 60밀리그램을 복용하는 환자를 치료 시작 시점보다 평균 약 3년 젊게 평가했습니다. 이러한 변화는 플라세보에 비해 통계적으로 유의미했습니다. 그러나 사망 위험을 예측하도록 훈련된 두 시계는 4주차에 해당 용량에서 유의미한 변화를 보이지 않았습니다.
하루 두 번 30밀리그램(분할 용량 요법)을 복용한 환자들은 두 시계 유형 모두에서 가장 일관된 감소를 보였습니다. 예측 생물학적 나이 감소가 가장 큰 것은 4주 차에 나타났으며, 나머지 8주 동안은 거의 변화가 없었습니다.
이 결과는 환자의 혈액 단백질 프로필이 젊은 사람들과 더 유사해졌음을 의미합니다. 하지만 치료 환자가 젊음을 되찾았거나 더 오래 살았다는 것을 입증하지는 못합니다.

광범위한 노화 방지 효과가 있을까요? 시계 측정값을 넘어서, 연구진은 치료가 섬유증, 대사, 세포 스트레스 반응에 관여하는 단백질을 포함한 326가지 혈액 단백질 수치를 변화시켰다는 사실을 발견했습니다. 두 개의 고용량 그룹에서 대부분의 변화는 임상시험 내내 지속되었거나 치료 후반에 나타났으며, 이는 예측 연령이 정체된 후에도 약물이 환자의 생물학에 계속 영향을 미쳤음을 시사합니다.
연구진은 젊은 연령 추정에 가장 큰 영향을 준 단백질을 조사했습니다. 섬유증 관련 단백질인 LTBP2가 주요 기여자로 두드러졌습니다. 이 단백질은 여섯 시계 모두에서 사용되었는데, 이는 이들의 일치가 주로 약물의 섬유증 효과에 영향을 반영하는지, 노화 지연 전반을 반영하는 것인지 의문을 제기합니다.
낮은 연령 추정치가 섬유증 개선 이상을 반영하는지 알아보기 위해, 연구진은 예측 연령 변화와 폐 기능 변화를 비교했습니다. 두 검사는 서로 밀접하게 추적하지 않았습니다. 이는 폐 기능 개선만으로는 시계 변화를 설명하지 못할 수 있음을 시사하지만, 폐 기능이 IPF의 모든 측면을 모두 포괄하지는 않습니다.
연구팀은 치료 유발 단백질 변화를 영국 바이오뱅크에서 젊은 참가자와 노인 참가자 간 차이와 비교했습니다. 분할 투여에서는 노화와 관련된 단백질이 반대 방향으로 이동하는 경향이 있었습니다: 노인에서 높은 수치가 발견되는 단백질은 감소하는 경향이 있었고, 그 반대도 마찬가지였습니다. 이 패턴은 단일 하루 용량에서는 통계적으로 유의미하지 않았습니다.
마지막으로, 연구진은 세포 노화세포와 관련된 단백질을 조사했습니다. 이 단백질들은 플라세보 그룹에서는 증가하는 경향이 있지만 치료 중에는 감소하는 경향이 있어, 렌토세르티브가 노화세포 관련 활성을 줄일 수 있음을 시사하지만, 연구진은 조직 내 노화 세포를 직접 측정하지는 않았습니다.
이러한 발견은 렌토서티브가 잠재적인 노인 보호제로서 연구할 수 있는 근거를 강화합니다. 그러나 섬유증, 대사, 노화세포가 밀접하게 연관되어 있기 때문에, 이 약물이 IPF의 이점 외에 노화에 영향을 미치는지 확정하지는 못합니다.
"이 연구는 노화 바이오마커가 기존 임상시험에 어떻게 통합될 수 있는지를 보여줍니다."라고 하버드 의과대학 의학 교수이자 이 연구의 공동 저자인 바딤 글라디셰프는 라이프스팬 뉴스에 말했습니다. "이러한 접근법이 더 폭넓게 검증된다면, 치료가 특정 질병에 영향을 미치는지뿐만 아니라 노화 생물학의 일부 측면에 영향을 미치는지도 알 수 있을 것입니다."

작은 부탁을 드리고 싶습니다. 저희는 비영리 재단이며, 다른 일부 단체와 달리 주주도 없고 판매할 제품도 없습니다. 모든 뉴스와 교육 콘텐츠는 누구나 무료로 읽을 수 있지만, 이는 여러분 같은 분들의 도움에 의존한다는 의미이기도 합니다. 크고 작음에 상관없이 모든 기부는 독립적이고 윤리적인 저널리즘을 지원하며 우리의 미래를 지탱합니다. 네, 저는 문학을❤️ 기부하겠습니다 [1] Zhavoronkov, A., Galkin, F., Chen, S., Ren, F., Aliper, A., Durymanov, M., ... 그리고 Gladyshev, V. N. (2026). 2a상 임상시험에서 단백질체 노화 시계 통합은 동시 노인 보호 평가를 지원합니다. Nature Biotechnology, 1-13.

[2] Argentieri, M. A., Xiao, S., Bennett, D., Winchester, L., Nevado-Holgado, A. J., Ghose, U., ... & van Duijn, C. M. (2024). 단백질체 노화 시계는 다양한 인구에서 흔한 연령 관련 질환의 사망률과 위험을 예측합니다. Nature medicine, 30(9), 2450-2460.
[3] Xu, Z., Ren, F., Wang, P., Cao, J., Tan, C., Ma, D., ... & Zhavoronkov, A. (2025). 특발성 폐섬유증을 위한 생성형 AI 발견 TNIK 억제제: 무작위 2a상 임상시험. Nature medicine, 31(8), 2602-2610.
[4] 에발트, C. Y., 풀로우스, F. E., 록, S. W. Y., 푼, F. W., 알리퍼, A., 렌, F., & 자보론코프, A. (2024). TNIK의 암, 대사 및 연령 관련 질환에서의 신흥 역할. 약리학 동향, 45(6), 478-489.

articles.titleOriginal: Your Personal Longevity Assistant: Evipedia Grok Bot
articles.summaryOriginal: With Grok Bot, SpaceXAi has created something really special and helpful. And the Evipedia Grok Bot turns this gem into something even more precious. A specialized AI assistant offering an evidence-based 2nd opinion on health and longevity interventions. It integrates Grok, the AI4L […]

bodyOriginal.text: With Grok Bot , SpaceXAi has created something really special and helpful. And the Evipedia Grok Bot turns this gem into something even more precious. A specialized AI assistant offering an evidence-based 2nd opinion on health and longevity interventions.
It integrates Grok, the AI4L persona , the Evipedia MCP server , and Evipedia-hosted search into one super-useful companion.

What Evipedia Grok Bot will do for you The bot will allow you to have interactive conversations about a wide range of health and longevity interventions. It delivers helpful 2nd opinions on these topics, and all its answers are grounded in the same principles and behavior used by Evipedia and AI4L:

Tailored for the Longevity Community — answers are framed for risk-aware adults actively optimizing their health, not for the general population Evidence First — conclusions rest on human clinical trials and meta-analyses; conflicting, thin, or absent evidence is named as such rather than smoothed over Graded Findings — each benefit and risk carries an explicit High, Medium, Low, or Speculative grade and, where the literature supports one, a magnitude The Full Picture — interventions are looked at across mechanism, benefits, risks, interactions, protocol, monitoring, and open research Commercial Interests — when the evidence comes from parties with a financial stake in the intervention, or from an organization whose members profit from the position it endorses, conflicts are named on every side of the debate Evipedia Lookup — health and longevity questions are checked against the evidence reviews on evipedia.ai before the model answers from memory Plain Language — acronyms and jargon get a short explanation at first use, and scientific nomenclature follows field convention Verified Links — every PMID, NCT ID, and DOI is retrieved and checked before it is shown; a URL that cannot be verified is omitted rather than guessed Review Suggestions — when an intervention under sustained discussion has no Evipedia review, the model offers to suggest it to the Evipedia editorial team or points to generating an evidence review using the AI4L prompt What’s in Evipedia Evipedia is a comprehensive, continuously updated online encyclopedia that provides much-needed, accurate, and up-to-date information on a wide range of health and longevity-related interventions.

Free to Use — Evipedia is completely free to use and open to everyone. We built Evipedia as a backbone tool for the whole longevity and rejuvenation community. Our goal is to empower individuals with knowledge to make informed decisions about their health and longevity. 770+ Evidence Reviews — Including whole-body therapies, brain health, skin rejuvenation, hormone optimization, peptides, psychedelics, medications, blood and plasma therapies, complementary cancer approaches, foundational habits, diets, foods, probiotics, botanicals, isolates, and many more. A Dual Structure for Every Entry — Each intervention has a one-page Quick Reference Sheet for an at-a-glance protocol, benefits, risks, contraindications, and monitoring, plus a Full Evidence Review for in-depth analysis. Continuous Updates — Entries are continuously updated to reflect the latest developments in health and longevity. On average, reviews are refreshed every 4-6 weeks, ensuring access to the most current information available. Full Audit and Quality Transparency — Every “Quick Reference Sheet” and “Evidence Review” on Evipedia includes an Audit Report that outlines the detailed audit criteria and the history of audits and fixes applied to the documents. Stable Permalinks – Beautiful Sharing Cards — Every intervention has a fixed, short URL and a purpose-designed social sharing card — ideal for citing a compound in a supplement stack or anchoring a claim in an online discussion. AI & Agent-friendly, Extensive Integration Support — Built as a backbone service for the longevity and rejuvenation community, Evipedia features a wide variety of AI integration tools and an easily accessible API . All are free to use, under an AI- and agent-friendly site policy and the Creative Commons 4.0 license. Built on AI4L — Evipedia is built on top of our open-source AI4L framework , which enables anyone to create high-quality, evidence-based reviews of health and longevity interventions. At the core of AI4L is our novel “ Audit-Driven Prompting ” approach to generate hallucination-free, accurate, and well-structured reviews using frontier AI models. About Forever Healthy Forever Healthy Foundation is a private, humanitarian initiative with the mission of enabling people to vastly extend their healthy lifespan. More at forever-healthy.org

bodyOriginal.text: Dezeen Showroom: from pieces designed to blend into the background to others that make a visual statement, the following storage products conceal clutter within capacious forms.
These products come from the catalogues of global design brands, including those based in Denmark , Italy, the UK, Germany, South Korea and Poland.
The selection includes cabinets , cupboards, sideboards , and storage systems, both built-in and freestanding, available in neutral and pop colourways.
Dezeen Showroom publishes furnishings and products designed and manufactured by international design brands.

bodyOriginal.alt: Wardrobes and storage by Reform

bodyOriginal.text: Danish brand Reform 's wardrobes and storage have a slimline and fully customisable appearance, both inside and out.
Optional add-ons include accessories, drawers and organisers, with units varying in capacity, dimension and exterior colour, from natural neutrals to vivid block colours.
Find out more about Reform's wardrobes and storage ›

bodyOriginal.alt: Container sideboard by E-ggs for Miniforms

bodyOriginal.text: Container sideboard by E-ggs for Miniforms
Italian furniture brand Miniforms worked with design studio E-ggs on this sideboard, which has a rigid front and is raised on slim legs at each corner.
The exterior of the ContainerUP and ContainerMID sideboards comes in wooden or lacquered finishes, with users able to choose different colours for different elements to encourage personalisation.

bodyOriginal.alt: MultiDrawer storage by Bisley

bodyOriginal.text: British workplace brand Bisley 's MultiDrawer storage items are timeless thanks to their minimalist design and durability.
The filing cabinet-like pieces come in various colourways, heights and sizes, including limited edition ranges.

bodyOriginal.alt: Stripes storage system by Jehs + Laub for Schönbuch

bodyOriginal.text: Stripes storage system by Jehs + Laub for Schönbuch
New finishes and accent colours are available for German furniture brand Schönbuch and designers Jehs + Laub's Stripes storage system .
Named after the linear recesses in its fronts that act as handles, the system comprises freestanding and built-in modules that can be tailored to existing interiors.

bodyOriginal.alt: DOB Modular System by Flat Point

bodyOriginal.text: South Korean brand Flat Point 's DOB Modular System is made up of moveable elements ranging from side and console tables of various sizes and colours.
All pieces are made from aluminium and feature both open shelving alongside cupboards and drawers.

bodyOriginal.alt: Original Modern Shelving by Tylko

bodyOriginal.text: Polish design brand Tylko invited users to utilise an online configurator to design their own storage systems made up of modules in the brand's Original Modern Shelving range.
From individual TV stands to full interior fit-outs, the system comes in a spectrum of colours and includes bookcases, sideboards, chests of drawers, vinyl storage and shoe racks.
Find out more about Original Modern Shelving ›

bodyOriginal.text: Have you ever imagined a pear or an apple with a personality? If the fruit suddenly had two eyes and a stem-like nose, it might look a little like PÉPET , the palm-size “paper friend” produced by TAKEO Co., Ltd. Originally designed by Masae Nagao , the colorful characters come with names like “Dandel,” “Fuji,” and “Sky.” They’re each composed of more than 400 of layers of colorful paper, and they adorably wobble and ruffle when handled.
Inspired by the saturated red and green of apples and their leaves, TAKEO will release a new edition named “Pomme” on October 14. Follow updates on the company’s Instagram .

The studio designed the 225-square-metre holiday home for a family to use either alone or with guests. Located on the Yatsugatake mountain plateau in central Japan, the The post Keiji Ashizawa cl

bodyOriginal.text: An "angled, folded form" clad in charred cedar defines this holiday home , designed by Japanese studio Keiji Ashizawa Design to embrace the surrounding landscape while maintaining its inhabitants' privacy.
The studio designed the 225-square-metre holiday home for a family to use either alone or with guests.
Located on the Yatsugatake mountain plateau in central Japan, the house has an unusual shape that was designed to suit its surroundings.

bodyOriginal.alt: House in forest

bodyOriginal.text: It was designed with an angled shape "Although surrounded by abundant nature, the site sits within a residential area of holiday homes," studio founder Keiji Ashizawa told Dezeen.
"The house was carefully positioned and shaped to remain open to the surrounding landscape while avoiding direct views toward neighbouring properties," Ashizawa continued.
"The placement of the windows follows the same approach, framing nature while maintaining a sense of privacy."

bodyOriginal.alt: Charred-wood house

bodyOriginal.text: Charred cedar wood clads the exterior The one-storey building has a gentle bend that creates angles that enclose its garden.

"In response to the surrounding views, the movement of natural light, and the scale of the house in relation to the landscape, an angled, folded form was developed to sit naturally within the site," Ashizawa said.

bodyOriginal.alt: Window to forest

bodyOriginal.text: Oak wood was used for the interior of House in Yatsugatake House in Yatsugatake was clad in yakisugi, a traditional Japanese charred cedar. The material was allowed to be used because the home is not in a densely populated area, where Japan has strict fire regulations.
"Unlike in central Tokyo, timber cladding is permitted in this area, allowing yakisugi to form an integral part of the exterior expression," Ashizawa said.

bodyOriginal.alt: Living room with large windows

bodyOriginal.text: The studio left wood beams exposed inside Ashizawa's studio also took the climate of the region into consideration when designing the house, which is located close to the road and also contains a garage.
"The house rests on a concrete foundation that becomes more exposed as the ground falls away across the sloping site," Ashizawa said.

Read: Keiji Ashizawa creates holiday home within historic machiya "Its relatively high profile also responds to the winter snowfall of Yatsugatake, following a construction approach commonly found in timber houses in colder regions," Ashizawa continued.
The holiday home has a central entrance, with a living, dining and kitchen area, loft and guest room in the western wing and private rooms and bathrooms to the east.

bodyOriginal.alt: Living room with mezzanine

bodyOriginal.text: The living room has a mezzanine floor Keiji Ashizawa Design used oak wood for the interior, which features exposed sloping beams and windows close to the roof that frame the garden.
A skylight above the mezzanine loft lets light into the living room area.
To create a connection with the garden, the studio added full-width timber-framed windows in the bathroom that give panoramic views of the surrounding forest.

bodyOriginal.alt: Bathroom with garden view

bodyOriginal.text: The bathroom has views over the forest "By carefully reading the existing topography, trees, light, and wind, and allowing the architecture to respond quietly to them, we sought to create a home in which the surrounding landscape gradually reveals itself over time," the studio said.
Keiji Ashizawa Design has previously created an eight-room Tokyo hotel and a holiday home in a historic machiya .

articles.titleKo: 아시자와 케이지가 야츠가타케의 집을 그을린 삼나무로 덮고 있다
articles.summaryKo: 그을린 삼나무로 덮인 '각지고 접힌 형태'가 이 휴양 주택을 정의하며, 일본 스튜디오 케이지 아시자와 디자인이 주변 경관을 포용하면서도 거주자의 사생활을 지키도록 설계했습니다. 스튜디오는 가족이 혼자 또는 손님과 함께 사용할 수 있도록 225제곱미터 규모의 휴양 주택을 설계했습니다. 일본 중부 야츠가타케 산악 고원에 위치한 케이지 아시자와 클
bodyKo: 그을린 삼나무로 덮인 '각진 접힌 형태'가 이 휴가용 주택을 정의하며, 일본 스튜디오 아시자와 케이지 디자인이 주변 경관을 포용하면서도 거주자의 사생활을 지키도록 설계했습니다.
스튜디오는 가족이 혼자 또는 손님과 함께 사용할 수 있도록 225제곱미터 규모의 휴가용 주택을 설계했습니다.
일본 중부 야츠가타케 산악 고원에 위치한 이 집은 주변 환경에 맞게 독특한 형태를 가지고 있습니다.
이 부지는 비스듬한 형태로 설계되었으며, "풍부한 자연으로 둘러싸여 있지만, 이 부지는 휴양 주택 주거 지역 내에 위치해 있다"고 스튜디오 창립자 아시자와 케이지가 Dezeen에 말했다.
"집은 주변 경관과 개방된 상태를 유지하면서도 인근 부동산을 직접 바라보지 않도록 신중하게 배치되고 형태가 형성되었습니다," 아시자와가 계속 말했다.
"창문 배치도 같은 방식을 따르며, 자연을 감싸면서도 사생활 보호를 유지합니다."
외관에는 그을린 삼나무 목재가 덮여 있습니다. 1층 건물은 완만한 굽기를 하여 정원을 둘러싸는 각도를 만듭니다.
"주변 경관, 자연광의 움직임, 그리고 집이 풍경과 비교한 규모에 대응하여, 부지 내에 자연스럽게 자리 잡을 수 있도록 기울고 접힌 형태가 개발되었습니다,"라고 아시자와는 말했습니다.
야츠가타케 주택 내부에는 참나무가 사용되었으며, 야츠가타케의 집은 전통 일본의 그을린 삼나무인 야키스기로 외장되었습니다. 이 재료는 일본의 엄격한 화재 규제가 있는 인구 밀집 지역에 있지 않기 때문에 사용이 허용되었습니다.
"도쿄 중심부와 달리 이 지역에서는 목재 외장재가 허용되어 야키스기가 외부 표현의 필수적인 부분이 될 수 있다"고 아시자와는 말했다.
스튜디오는 아시자와의 스튜디오 내부에 나무 들보를 노출시켰으며, 도로 근처에 위치한 이 집에는 차고도 포함되어 있어 지역 기후도 고려했습니다.
"집은 경사진 부지를 따라 땅이 떨어질수록 더 노출되는 콘크리트 기초 위에 세워져 있다"고 아시자와는 말했다.
읽어보기: 아시자와 케이지, 역사적인 마치야 내에 휴가용 주택을 설계하다 "비교적 높은 프로필은 추운 지역의 목재 주택에서 흔히 볼 수 있는 건축 방식을 따르며, 야츠가타케의 겨울 눈에도 반응한다"고 아시자와는 덧붙였다.
휴양 주택은 중앙 출입구를 갖추고 있으며, 서쪽 날개에는 거실, 식당, 주방 공간, 다락방과 게스트룸, 동쪽에는 개인실과 욕실이 있습니다.
거실은 케이지 아시자와 디자인이 내부에 사용한 오크 목재를 사용한 중이층 바닥으로, 정원을 감싸는 지붕 가까이에 노출된 경사진 들보와 창문이 특징입니다.
중이층 다락방 위의 천창이 거실 공간으로 빛을 들여옵니다.
정원과의 연결을 위해 스튜디오는 욕실에 전폭 목조 창문을 추가하여 주변 숲의 파노라마 전망을 제공했습니다.
욕실에서는 숲이 조망할 수 있습니다. "기존 지형, 나무, 빛, 바람을 세심하게 읽고, 건축물이 조용히 반응하도록 허용함으로써, 시간이 지남에 따라 주변 풍경이 점차 드러나는 집을 만들고자 했습니다,"라고 스튜디오는 말했습니다.
케이지 아시자와 디자인은 이전에 도쿄에 8개 객실의 호텔과 역사적인 매치야에 휴양지를 만든 바 있습니다.

bodyOriginal.text: Atherosclerosis is the largest cause of human mortality, producing stroke and heart attack when fatty plaques obstructing arteries rupture. There is accordingly a great deal of research aimed at influencing the course of the condition. Reversal of plaque growth to clear arteries and remove potentially unstable plaques remains a challenge, and few approaches have been shown to achieve this goal with any reliability even in animal studies. Conversely, many different approaches have been shown to slow the development of atherosclerosis in high fat diet mouse models of the condition. The example here is a demonstration of the degree to which maladaptive fat tissue metabolism contributes to the environment of inflammation and cell stress that accelerates the growth of atherosclerotic plaque. Unfortunately, like so many other approaches, reducing inflammation (via many different means) has not been shown to significantly regress established plaque in and of itself.

Adipocyte dysfunction is closely associated with oxidative stress and chronic inflammation , which contribute to systemic metabolic disturbances and atherosclerosis. We previously identified the NKA (Na/K-ATPase) α1 subunit as a signal transducer that activates Src-family kinases and promotes oxidative stress and inflammation in various cell types, including adipocytes and macrophages . NaKtide , a peptide inhibitor of NKA signaling, has been shown to reduce systemic oxidative stress and inflammation in vivo . In this study, we investigated the role of adipocyte-specific NKA signaling in atherosclerosis.

Adipocyte-specific NaKtide was delivered to Apoe-/- mice using a lentiviral vector under the adiponectin promoter . The mice were then fed a Western diet for 12 weeks to induce atherosclerosis and then assessed for atherosclerotic plaque burden in the aortic arch and at the level of the aortic sinus . Inflammatory and oxidative stress markers were analyzed in adipose tissue and plasma . Adipocyte-specific NaKtide reduced atherosclerotic plaque area by 67% in the aortic arch and by 48% in the aortic sinus. CD68 + macrophage content and α-SMA + smooth muscle cell content in the aortic sinus were decreased by 45% and 53%, respectively. These vascular improvements were accompanied by dampened adipose tissue inflammation and oxidative stress, improved glucose tolerance , and reduced systemic inflammation.

These findings highlight a critical contributing role for adipocyte NKA signaling in atherosclerosis, suggesting an important endocrine and paracrine influence of adipose tissue on large artery atherogenesis and supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting NKA in cardiometabolic disease.
Link: https://doi.org/10.1161/ATVBAHA.126.325070

articles.author: Reason
articles.titleKo: 죽상동맥경화에 기여하는 지방 세포에 의한 염증
articles.summaryKo: 동맥경화증은 동맥을 막는 지방 플라크가 파열될 때 뇌졸중과 심장마비를 일으키는 인간 사망의 가장 큰 원인입니다. 따라서 이 질환의 경과에 영향을 미치기 위한 많은 연구가 이루어지고 있습니다. 동맥을 정화하고 잠재적으로 불안정한 플라크를 제거하기 위한 플라크 성장을 되돌리는 일은 여전히 도전 과제이며, 이를 달성할 수 있는 접근법은 거의 제시되지 않았습니다
bodyKo: 죽상동맥경화증은 동맥을 막는 지방 플라크가 파열될 때 뇌졸중과 심장마비를 일으키는 인간 사망의 가장 큰 원인입니다. 따라서 이 질환의 경과에 영향을 미치기 위한 많은 연구가 진행되고 있습니다. 동맥을 정화하고 잠재적으로 불안정한 플라크를 제거하기 위한 플라크 성장 역전은 여전히 도전 과제이며, 동물 연구에서도 신뢰성 있게 이 목표를 달성한 접근법은 거의 없습니다. 반대로, 고지방 식이요법 마우스 모델에서 죽상동맥경화증 발생을 늦추는 다양한 접근법이 입증되었습니다. 여기 예시는 부적응 지방 조직 대사가 염증 환경과 세포 스트레스에 얼마나 기여하여 죽상경화성 플라크의 성장을 가속화하는지를 보여줍니다. 안타깝게도, 다른 많은 접근법과 마찬가지로, 다양한 방법으로 염증을 줄여도 기존 플라크를 현저히 퇴보시키는 것으로 입증되지 않았습니다.

지방세포 기능 장애는 산화 스트레스 및 만성 염증과 밀접한 관련이 있으며, 이는 전신 대사 장애와 동맥경화증에 기여합니다. 우리는 이전에 NKA(Na/K-ATPase) α1 소단위를 Src 계열 키나아제를 활성화하고 지방세포와 대식세포를 포함한 다양한 세포 유형에서 산화 스트레스와 염증을 촉진하는 신호 전달자로 확인했습니다. NAKTIDE는 NKA 신호 전달의 펩타이드 억제제로, 생체 내에서 전신 산화 스트레스와 염증을 감소시키는 것으로 나타났습니다. 본 연구에서는 지방세포 특이적 NKA 신호전달이 동맥경화증에서 어떤 역할을 하는지 조사했습니다.

지방세포 특이적 NaKtide는 아디포넥틴 프로모터 하에 렌티바이러스 벡터를 사용해 Apoe-/- 마우스에 전달하였다. 이후 쥐들은 12주간 웨스턴 식단을 먹여 죽상동맥경화를 유도한 후, 대동맥궁과 대동맥동동 수준에서 동맥경화성 플라크 부하를 평가하였다. 지방 조직과 혈장에서 염증 및 산화 스트레스 지표를 분석하였다. 지방세포 특이적 NaKtide는 대동맥궁에서 죽상동맥경화성 플라크 면적을 67%, 대동맥동에서 48% 감소시켰다. 대동맥동에서 CD68+대식세포 함량과 α-SMA + 평활근 세포 함량은 각각 45%, 53% 감소하였다. 이러한 혈관 개선은 지방 조직 염증과 산화 스트레스 완화, 포도당 내성 개선, 전신 염증 감소와 함께 이루어졌습니다.
이 발견들은 죽상동맥경화에서 지방세포 NKA 신호전달이 중요한 역할을 한다는 점을 강조하며, 지방 조직이 큰 동맥 동맥 형성에 중요한 내분비 및 부분비적 영향을 미친다는 것을 시사하고, 심장대사 질환에서 NKA를 표적으로 하는 치료 잠재력을 지지합니다.
링크: https://doi.org/10.1161/ATVBAHA.126.325070

articles.titleOriginal: Aging is Complex, So Expect High Variance in the Details Between Individuals
articles.summaryOriginal: Aging is a complex stochastic process of damage accumulation, shaped at the detail level by choices made, environments encountered, and the responses and interactions of countless cells. bodyOriginal.text: Aging is a complex stochastic process of damage accumulation , shaped at the detail level by choices made, environments encountered, and the responses and interactions of countless cells. As the paper here notes, this gives rise to a sizable variance between individuals, even those with the same genetics or similar lifestyles. The research and medical community largely react to this variance with a drive towards developing personalized medicine , but the underlying mechanisms of aging are the same from individual to individual, even if outcomes vary. A therapy that addresses one underlying mechanism in one tissue will tend to produce differing levels of benefit from person to person, but in principle it should always produce benefit. Undergoing some degree of repair should always result in better outcomes than not undergoing repair.

Most human omic studies remain cross-sectional , despite growing evidence that transcriptomic and metabolomic states are temporally dynamic. Cross-sectional designs are limited in their capacity to separate stable interindividual differences from within-participant change and may obscure the degree to which molecular aging varies between individuals. Longitudinal multiomic studies address this gap but are challenging to implement. To address these challenges, we established the MultiMuTHER study within the deeply phenotyped TwinsUK cohort . MultiMuTHER includes repeated whole-blood RNA sequencing and serum metabolomic profiling at three or more time points over up to 8 years in 335 females. We used this resource to ask four questions: which genes and metabolites change over time; how much individual trajectories diverge from population-level trends; to what extent multiomic trajectories are shaped by intrinsic factors including host genetics and cell type composition as well as extrinsic elements such as circadian timing, seasonality, and environmental exposures; and whether transcriptomic and metabolomic changes are coordinated across omic layers.

We identified 5,061 genes and 181 metabolites whose levels changed over time, with participants displaying distinct longitudinal trajectories, sometimes opposite to population-level trends. Longitudinal changes in gene expression exhibited marked cell type specificity, with different patterns in the adaptive versus innate immune compartments. Longitudinally variable genes were enriched for functional categories relevant to aging, including cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative disorders. Gene expression and metabolite levels showed strong context-specificity, with 25% of genes and 24% of metabolites associated with seasonality, and 26 and 39%, respectively, associated with circadian variation.

Our findings show molecular aging to be a dynamic, context-dependent, and highly individualized process. Longitudinal multiomic profiling revealed molecular changes shared across the population and trajectories that diverged between individuals, while highlighting the influence of cell type composition, host genetics, biological rhythms, environmental exposures, and cross-omic connectivity. This study, along with the MultiMuTHER resource, provides a framework for understanding biological aging as a set of interacting molecular trajectories, with utility for future precision medicine efforts.
Link: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aed6452

articles.author: Reason
articles.titleKo: 노화는 복잡하기 때문에 개인마다 세부적인 차이가 크다고 예상하세요
articles.summaryKo: 노화는 선택, 마주치는 환경, 수많은 세포의 반응과 상호작용에 의해 세부 수준에서 형성되는 복잡한 확률적 손상 축적 과정입니다. 논문에서 지적하듯, 이는 동일한 유전자나 유사한 생활방식을 가진 사람들 사이에서도 상당한 차이를 초래합니다. 연구와 의학계는 주로 이 차이에 대해 다음과 같이 반응합니다.
bodyKo: 노화는 선택, 마주친 환경, 수많은 세포의 반응과 상호작용에 의해 세부 수준에서 형성되는 복잡한 확률적 손상 축적 과정입니다. 논문에서 지적했듯이, 이는 동일한 유전이나 유사한 생활방식을 가진 사람들 사이에서도 상당한 차이를 초래합니다. 연구와 의료계는 주로 개인 맞춤형 의학 개발을 추진하며 이러한 변동에 반응하지만, 노화의 근본 메커니즘은 결과가 다를 수 있지만 개인마다 동일합니다. 한 조직의 한 기전을 다루는 치료는 개인마다 이득 수준이 다르지만, 원칙적으로는 항상 이득을 가져야 합니다. 어느 정도 수리를 받는 것이 항상 수리를 받지 않는 것보다 더 나은 결과를 가져야 합니다.

대부분의 인간 오믹 연구는 전사체 및 대사체 상태가 시간적으로 동적이라는 증거가 증가함에 따라 횡단적으로 유지되고 있습니다. 횡단면 설계는 안정적인 개인간 차이와 참가자 내 변화를 구분하는 데 한계가 있으며, 분자 노화가 개인별로 얼마나 다양한지를 가릴 수 있습니다. 종단 다중체학 연구는 이 격차를 해결하지만 구현이 어렵습니다. 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 우리는 심층 표현형이 있는 TwinsUK 코호트 내에서 MultiMuTHER 연구를 설립했습니다. MultiMuTHER는 335명의 여성을 대상으로 최대 8년에 걸쳐 3개 이상의 시점에서 반복적으로 전혈 RNA 시퀀싱과 혈청 대사체 프로파일링을 포함합니다. 우리는 이 자료를 활용해 네 가지 질문을 던졌습니다: 어떤 유전자와 대사산물이 시간에 따라 변하는지; 개별 경로가 집단 수준 추세와 얼마나 차이나는지; 다중체 경로가 숙주 유전과 세포 유형 구성 같은 내재적 요인뿐만 아니라 일주기 타이밍, 계절성, 환경 노출과 같은 외부 요소에 의해 형성되는지; 그리고 전사체 및 대사체 변화가 옴 계층 간에 조정되는지 여부.

우리는 5,061개의 유전자와 181개의 대사산물을 확인했으며, 이들은 시간이 지남에 따라 수치가 변하는 것으로 나타났으며, 참가자들은 때때로 집단 수준 추세와 반대되는 뚜렷한 종단 경로를 보였습니다. 유전자 발현의 종단 변화는 적응 면역 구획과 선천 면역 구획에서 서로 다른 패턴을 보인 뚜렷한 세포 유형 특이성을 보였습니다. 종방향으로 변하는 유전자들은 심장대사 및 신경퇴행성 질환을 포함한 노화와 관련된 기능 범주에 대해 풍부하게 증가했습니다. 유전자 발현과 대사물 수준은 강한 맥락 특이성을 보였으며, 각각 25%의 유전자와 24%의 대사산물이 계절성과 연관되었고, 26%와 39%는 생체 변동과 관련이 있었습니다.

우리의 연구 결과는 분자 노화가 역동적이고 맥락에 의존적이며 매우 개별화된 과정임을 보여줍니다. 종단적 다중종체 프로파일링은 인구 집단 전반에 걸쳐 분자 변화가 공유되고 개인별로 다른 경로가 있음을 밝혀내며, 세포 유형 구성, 숙주 유전학, 생물학적 리듬, 환경 노출, 교차 옴 연결성의 영향을 강조했습니다. 이 연구와 MultiMuTHER 자료는 생물학적 노화를 상호작용하는 분자 궤적의 집합으로 이해할 수 있는 틀을 제공하며, 향후 정밀 의학 연구에 유용함을 제공합니다.
링크: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aed6452

articles.titleOriginal: How London designers are making it work
articles.summaryOriginal: London may have a lot to shout about design-wise, but is it actually possible to survive as a creative in one of the world's most expensive cities? Ahead of London Design Festival, we spoke to five local designers about the challenges they face. "I'm willing to live very modestly" said Tessa Silva "Financially, I've had The post How London designers are making it work appeared first on Dezeen .

bodyOriginal.text: London may have a lot to shout about design-wise, but is it actually possible to survive as a creative in one of the world's most expensive cities? Ahead of London Design Festival , we spoke to five local designers about the challenges they face.

bodyOriginal.alt: Portrait and fabric designs by Tessa Silva

bodyOriginal.text: Left photo by Kane Hulse, middle photo by Benedict Brink, right photo by Will Edgecombe "I'm willing to live very modestly" said Tessa Silva

"Financially, I've had the toughest start to the year that I've had in the 10 years since graduating. I was teaching and assisting another artist before, I had my finger in a couple of other pies, but I let it all fall by the wayside. I suddenly found myself in a position where I didn't have anything to fall back on. It's taught me I have to keep connections with people and let them know I can still work for them, even if it seems like I have a big commission.

"Any time I do make money, I put it back into making new things in my studio. I'm willing to live very modestly, and hopefully that pays off one day. I don't buy new clothes or go out for dinner a lot; I make my own packed lunches. I live in a small flat that I've made beautiful – that's just part of choosing to live in London.

"A good currency for designers is doing swaps with people. I've gotten a photographer to photograph my work because I've given them a piece of my furniture, or I've got some nice jewellery because I've swapped it for work. It's a way of owning a few precious things when you can't afford to pay upfront for them.

"Even though this year has been really hard, I've been getting a few bites this summer that are making me excited and make me think this could be something long term and sustainable for the future, which is a really nice feeling."
Tessa Silva is exhibiting at Max Radford Gallery 's Progressive Permanence

bodyOriginal.alt: Portrait and chair designs by Jake Robertson

bodyOriginal.text: Left and right photos by Jake Robertson, middle photo courtesy of Slancha "You find nifty ways of transporting wood when you're going on a bike everywhere" said Jake Robertson

"Work for a designer who's got plenty of work for you to do, and they might be keen for you to use their workshop in your spare time – that's what James Shaw has done for me. I had to get inventive and learn how to make stuff that can fold up, disappear, and slip into the cracks of the workshop so I'm not taking up someone's space. It does mean you've got to graft outside of work and on the weekend, but it gave me access to great machinery.

"A great place to go for cheap offcut materials is Renée Materials. You'll find stuff there that you would never think could make furniture. I cycle – I'm not paying for transport, I can't do it – but you find nifty ways of transporting wood when you're going on a bike everywhere.

"I don't really make money from my practice. I've sold a couple of things, but it's not a money-making business. Hopefully one day I can get there, but that's a reason I would suggest people work part-time or full-time for a designer. I don't have to keep pumping my own work out. I also need a job that pays the rent. I can make good work and keep putting those things out – I don't need to dilute my Instagram by constantly putting stuff out for likes when that doesn't equal more sales."
Jake Robertson is exhibiting at Out of Worky and Design Everything's With Limitations

bodyOriginal.alt: Portrait and lamp designs by Hanna Fastrich

bodyOriginal.text: Left and middle photos by Findlay Macdonald, right photo by Jasper Jones "My hack is trying to overcome my feeling of cringe" said Hanna Fastrich

"There are a lot of challenges in London, but it's a super-rich environment, and what's most important to me is my community. I have friends from uni or group exhibitions that are also designers, and we support each other. I work on ceramics and metal in my workshop, and sometimes I want to do some wood or something else, which a friend can give me access to. There's a beautiful sharing economy in my community – there's no gatekeeping.

"I always intensely apply to open calls, prizes and grants. I get loads of rejections, but every once in a while you get a yes. In the beginning, it felt cringe to reach out to people or send an email with my portfolio to a gallery, so my hack is trying to overcome my feeling of cringe and not to think about the worst possible outcome. Someone could say no and reject you, but that's not a horrible outcome, it's just a numbers game in the end."
Hanna Fastrich is exhibiting at Slancha 's Hanging Baskets

bodyOriginal.alt: Portrait and stool designs by ThisIsByron

bodyOriginal.text: Photos by ThisIsByron "I turned to using waste materials as a necessity" said ThisIsByron

"My biggest overhead is material costs. That's how I turned to using waste materials – as a necessity. I then looked at what I could find within London and made a patchwork series with hardwood offcuts I found from various studios.
"I currently have a part-time job at the Royal Academy Schools as a workshop tutor. It's important I earn a wage that supports London living but also pays back into my studio.

"London is tricky, but it's also a bit of magic. Unit.d in Haggerston is like a church service affair where designers descend each month to hang out and share ideas – this only exists because of living in the city."
ThisIsByron is curating We Lift Each Other

bodyOriginal.alt: Portrait of and metalwork designs by Marc Sweeney

bodyOriginal.text: Left and right photos by Marc Sweeney, middle photo courtesy of Slancha "It's more valuable to have relationships with expert makers" said Marc Sweeney

"After I graduated in London, I moved back to Scotland and quickly discovered that I wasn't part of any design community. I may as well have been making work on the moon – there's just no point doing it if nobody's engaging with you.

"I am wrestling with the balance of being in London to network and work freelance, and I'm going to be teaching at Instituto Marangoni, then coming up to Scotland to make things. My family runs a passenger boat business on Loch Lomond, so we've got unbelievable workshop facilities. The long-term plan is to have a space in London, but it is eye-wateringly expensive – almost pretty much unaffordable for a single emerging designer.

"I'm a hands-on maker, but my work's got to a point where I need the help of experts. I'm outsourcing some work, or certain stages of my work. It's more valuable to have relationships with expert makers, which there are loads of in London, than it is to have your own space with machinery and you're trying to do absolutely everything yourself."
Marc Sweeney is exhibiting at Slancha's Hanging Baskets

This article was written as part of our Dezeen Dispatch magazine for LDF 2026. LDF 2026 is taking place at various locations around the city from 12 to 20 September. To see what's on, visit Dezeen Events Guide .

articles.author: Amy Peacock
articles.titleKo: 런던 디자이너들이 어떻게 이 게임을 해내고 있는가
articles.summaryKo: 런던은 디자인 분야에서 많은 이목을 가질 수 있지만, 세계에서 가장 비싼 도시 중 하나에서 창작자로서 살아남는 것이 과연 가능할까요? 런던 디자인 페스티벌을 앞두고 우리는 다섯 명의 지역 디자이너와 그들이 직면한 도전에 대해 이야기를 나누었습니다. "저는 매우 소박하게 살 의향이 있습니다"라고 테사 실바는 말했습니다. "재정적으로는, Dezeen에 처음 게재된 '런던 디자이너들이 어떻게 성공하고 있는가'라는 글이 처음 게재되었습니다.
bodyKo: 런던은 디자인 분야에서 많은 관심을 가질 수 있지만, 세계에서 가장 비싼 도시 중 하나에서 창작자로서 살아남는 것이 과연 가능할까요? 런던 디자인 페스티벌을 앞두고 우리는 다섯 명의 지역 디자이너와 그들이 직면한 도전에 대해 이야기를 나누었습니다.
왼쪽 사진: 케인 헐스, 가운데 사진: 베네딕트 브링크, 오른쪽 사진: 윌 에지콤브 "저는 매우 겸손하게 살 준비가 되어 있습니다"라고 테사 실바가 말했습니다.
"재정적으로는, 졸업한 지 10년 동안 가장 힘든 시작을 보냈어요. 전에 다른 예술가를 가르치고 도왔고, 몇몇 다른 일에도 관여했지만, 결국 모두 포기했어요. 갑자기 의지할 곳이 전혀 없는 상황에 처했죠. 사람들을 계속 연결하고, 비록 큰 의뢰가 있는 것처럼 보여도 여전히 그들과 일할 수 있다는 걸 알려줘야 한다는 걸 배웠어요.
"돈을 벌 때마다 다시 작업실에서 새로운 것을 만드는 데 쓰죠. 저는 매우 소박하게 살 준비가 되어 있고, 언젠가 그게 보상받길 바랍니다. 새 옷을 사거나 외식을 자주 하지 않아요; 직접 도시락을 싸서 싸요. 제가 아름답게 꾸민 작은 아파트에 살고 있어요 – 런던에 살기로 선택하는 이유 중 하나죠.
"디자이너들에게 좋은 화폐는 사람들과 교환하는 거야. 나는 내 가구를 사진작가에게 선물해준 사진작가에게 내 작품을 찍게 하거나, 내가 일과 교환해서 멋진 보석을 얻었어. 선불로 살 형편이 안 될 때 소중한 물건을 소유하는 방법이야.
"올해가 정말 힘들었지만, 이번 여름에 몇 입 먹는 게 기대되고, 이게 장기적이고 지속 가능한 일일 수 있을 것 같다는 생각이 들어서 정말 기분 좋아."
테사 실바는 맥스 래드포드 갤러리의 프로그레시브 퍼머넌스에서 전시 중입니다
왼쪽과 오른쪽 사진은 제이크 로버트슨이 촬영했으며, 가운데 사진은 슬란차가 제공했습니다. "자전거를 타고 어디든 다닐 때 나무를 운반하는 멋진 방법을 찾는다"고 제이크 로버트슨이 말했습니다

"디자이너 밑에서 일하는 거고, 그 디자이너는 네가 여가 시간에 그들의 작업장을 쓰길 원할 수도 있어. 그게 제임스 쇼가 나를 위해 해준 일이야. 나는 창의력을 발휘해서 접히고, 사라지고, 작업장 틈새로 미끄러져 들어가는 물건을 만드는 법을 배워야 했어. 그래야 누군가의 공간을 차지하지 않아. 물론 일할 때나 주말에도 노력해야 하지만, 좋은 기계를 사용할 수 있었어.
"저렴한 자재를 사기 좋은 곳은 르네 머티리얼이에요. 거기서는 가구를 만들 수 있을 거라 생각도 못 했던 물건들을 찾을 수 있어요. 저는 자전거를 타는데, 교통비는 내지 않아요, 할 수 없거든요 – 하지만 자전거를 타고 어디든 갈 때 나무를 운반하는 멋진 방법들을 찾게 되죠.

"저는 제 작업에서 돈을 많이 벌지는 않아요. 몇 가지 작품을 팔긴 했지만, 돈을 버는 사업은 아니에요. 언젠가는 그런 곳에 도달하길 바라지만, 그래서 사람들이 디자이너를 위해 파트타임이나 풀타임으로 일하라고 권하고 싶어요. 제 작업을 계속 쏟아낼 필요는 없고요. 월세를 낼 수 있는 일도 필요해요. 좋은 작품을 만들고 계속 그런 작품들을 낼 수 있어요 – 판매가 늘어나지 않을 때 계속 좋아요를 받으려고 인스타그램을 희석시킬 필요는 없어요."
제이크 로버트슨은 Out of Worky와 Design Everything's With Limitations에서 전시를 하고 있습니다
왼쪽과 중간 사진: 핀들레이 맥도날드, 오른쪽 사진: 재스퍼 존스 "내 허크는 내 민망함을 극복하려고 노력 중이야"라고 한나 패스트리치가 말했다
"런던에는 많은 도전이 있지만, 매우 부유한 환경이고, 저에게 가장 중요한 것은 제 커뮤니티입니다. 대학이나 단체전 친구들 중 디자이너도 있고, 서로 응원합니다. 작업실에서 도자기와 금속 작업을 하고, 가끔은 친구가 접근할 수 있는 나무나 다른 작업을 하고 싶을 때도 있습니다. 제 지역사회에는 아름다운 공유 경제가 있습니다 – 문지기가 없습니다.

"저는 항상 열심히 공모, 상, 보조금에 지원해요. 거절당하긴 하지만, 가끔은 '예'라는 답변을 받기도 해요. 처음에는 사람들에게 연락하거나 포트폴리오를 갤러리에 이메일로 보내는 게 민망하게 느껴졌어요. 그래서 제 해킹은 그 민망함을 극복하고 최악의 결과를 생각하지 않으려고 노력하고 있어요. 누군가가 거절하고 거절할 수도 있지만, 그게 끔찍한 결과는 아니고 결국 숫자 싸움일 뿐이에요."
한나 패스트리치는 슬란차의 행잉 바스켓츠에서 전시 중입니다
ThisIsByron의 사진 "저는 필요에 따라 폐기물을 사용하게 되었습니다"라고 ThisIsByron은 말했습니다
"가장 큰 간접비는 재료비입니다. 그래서 폐기물을 필수적으로 사용하기 시작했습니다. 그 후 런던에서 찾을 수 있는 것들을 살펴보고, 여러 스튜디오에서 찾은 원목 자재로 조각보 시리즈를 만들었습니다.
"현재 로열 아카데미 스쿨에서 워크숍 튜터로 파트타임으로 일하고 있습니다. 런던에서의 생활을 유지할 수 있는 임금을 벌면서 작업실에 대한 보답도 되는 것이 중요합니다.
"런던은 까다롭지만, 동시에 약간의 마법도 있어요. 해거스턴의 Unit.d는 마치 교회 예배 행사 같아서 디자이너들이 매달 와서 모여 아이디어를 나누는 거죠 – 이런 건 도시에서 살기 때문에 존재하는 거죠."
이게 바이런이 큐레이팅하는 '우리는 서로를 들어 올려요
왼쪽과 오른쪽 사진은 마크 스위니(Marc Sweeney), 중간 사진은 슬란차(Slancha) 제공 "전문가 제작자들과의 관계가 더 가치 있다고 마크 스위니는 말했습니다
"런던에서 졸업한 후 스코틀랜드로 돌아왔는데, 곧 제가 어떤 디자인 커뮤니티에도 속하지 않는다는 것을 알게 되었습니다. 달에서 작업을 하는 것과 다를 바 없었죠 – 아무도 당신과 소통하지 않는다면 아무 의미가 없으니까요.

"저는 런던에서 네트워킹과 프리랜서 활동을 하면서 균형을 맞추고 있습니다. 그리고 Instituto Marangoni에서 가르치고, 그 후 스코틀랜드로 와서 무언가를 만들 예정입니다. 저희 가족은 로흐 로몬드에서 여객선 사업을 운영하고 있어서, 믿을 수 없을 만큼 훌륭한 작업장 시설을 갖추고 있습니다. 장기적으로는 런던에 공간을 갖는 것이 계획이지만, 비용이 엄청나게 비싸서 신진 디자이너 한 명에게는 거의 감당하기 어려울 정도입니다.
"저는 직접 손으로 만드는 사람이지만, 제 작업은 전문가들의 도움이 필요할 정도입니다. 일부 작업이나 작업의 특정 단계를 외주주화하고 있습니다. 런던에는 전문가 제작자들과 관계를 맺는 것이 기계가 있는 자신의 공간을 갖고 모든 것을 혼자 하려는 것보다 더 가치 있습니다."
마크 스위니가 슬란차의 행잉 바스켓츠에서 전시를 하고 있습니다
이 기사는 LDF 2026을 위한 Dezeen Dispatch 매거진의 일부로 작성되었습니다. LDF 2026은 9월 12일부터 20일까지 도시 곳곳에서 열립니다. 행사 내용을 보시려면 Dezeen 이벤트 가이드를 방문하세요.
'런던 디자이너들이 어떻게 성공시키고 있는가'라는 글은 Dezeen에 처음 게재되었습니다.

articles.titleOriginal: From World Cup Champions to Longevity Champions
articles.summaryOriginal: Fresh from Spain’s spectacular victory in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Madrid is preparing for another kind of world-class gathering: one focused not on winning more years of sporting glory, but […]

bodyOriginal.text: Fresh from Spain’s spectacular victory in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Madrid is preparing for another kind of world-class gathering: one focused not on winning more years of sporting glory, but on winning more healthy years of life.

On September 30 and October 1, 2026, the International Longevity Summit Madrid 2026 will bring together leading scientists, physicians, entrepreneurs, investors and futurists to explore one of humanity’s greatest challenges—and potentially greatest opportunities: extending healthy human life.

Organized by the International Longevity Alliance, the Summit comes to a city uniquely positioned to lead the global conversation on longevity. Spain has the highest life expectancy in the European Union, while the Comunidad de Madrid has recorded the highest life expectancy of any EU region, reaching the remarkable landmark of 85.7 years according to Eurostat. Madrid may therefore be more than simply a great European capital; it could increasingly be considered a “Blue Zone 2.0”: a modern, dynamic metropolis where exceptional longevity meets cutting-edge science, biotechnology and innovation.

bodyOriginal.alt: LSM 2

bodyOriginal.text: And now, after Spain’s national team, La Roja, captured the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Spain can proudly claim another world-leading achievement. In July, Spain defeated Argentina 1–0 after extra time to win its second men’s World Cup title, adding a new chapter to a country already renowned for its health, lifestyle and longevity.

From world champions on the football field to potential champions of healthy longevity, Spain is demonstrating that the future may belong to those who know how to live—and perhaps someday live much longer.

bodyOriginal.alt: LSM 3

bodyOriginal.text: A new royal home at Spain’s most prestigious medical institution After the success of previous editions held at the Ilustre Colegio Oficial de Médicos de Madrid (ICOMEM), where the Summit was inaugurated with the participation of the Mayor of Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, the 2026 edition takes a major institutional step forward.

This year, the Summit will be held at the magnificent Real Academia Nacional de Medicina de España (RANME), the Royal National Academy of Medicine of Spain, the country’s most prestigious medical institution. Founded in 1734, the Academy occupies a unique place in Spanish scientific history. The Academy is under the High Patronage of His Majesty King Felipe VI, underlining the exceptional institutional importance of the venue. The Academy is also historically associated with some of the greatest names in medicine, including Spain’s Nobel laureates Santiago Ramón y Cajal and Severo Ochoa.

Located in the historic heart of Madrid, between the Royal Palace and the Teatro Real, the RANME will provide an extraordinary setting for a conversation that could reshape the future of medicine itself.

From George Church and Ray Kurzweil to Eric Topol and Peter Diamandis The International Longevity Summit has rapidly become a meeting point for some of the world’s most influential thinkers in longevity, biotechnology, medicine and the future of humanity.

Previous editions of the International Longevity Summit in Madrid have featured an exceptional roster of speakers, including George Church , pioneering geneticist; Ray Kurzweil , futurist and inventor; Steve Horvath , creator of the epigenetic clock; Andrea Maier , longevity physician and researcher; Mehmood Khan , global health and life sciences leader; Liz Parrish , biotechnology entrepreneur; Aubrey de Grey , biomedical gerontologist; Bryan Johnson , entrepreneur and longevity pioneer; María Blasco , molecular biologist and telomere researcher; João Pedro de Magalhães , biogerontologist and aging researcher; and Michael Ringel , biotechnology and pharmaceutical executive—along with many other leading scientists, physicians, entrepreneurs, and innovators from around the world.

The 2026 edition continues and expands this tradition of quality. Among the distinguished participants and speakers announced for 2026 are Eric Topol , cardiologist and digital medicine pioneer; Peter Diamandis , entrepreneur and futurist; Brian Kennedy , aging researcher; Valentin Fuster , cardiologist and cardiovascular scientist; Bashayer Almubarak , longevity and health innovation leader; Guido Kroemer , cell biologist and aging researcher; Steven Austad , biogerontologist; Michel Poulain , demographer and Blue Zones researcher; Michael West , stem cell pioneer; Mike Chan , longevity expert and entrepreneur; Wei-Wu He , biotechnology entrepreneur; Patrick E. Sewell , longevity physician; Ronald Bonilla , dentist and longevity innovator; Tina Woods , health and longevity leader; Daniel Wallerstorfer , geneticist and biotech entrepreneur; David Wood , futurist and longevity advocate; and Kenneth Scott , entrepreneur and longevity advocate—along with many other leading international and Spanish scientists, physicians, entrepreneurs, and innovators.

The program will span the biology of aging, rejuvenation biotechnology, preventive and regenerative medicine, artificial intelligence, health data, biomarkers, the longevity economy and the profound social consequences of potentially dramatic increases in human healthspan.

From conference to scientific marketplace: posters and startup pitches debut in 2026 For the first time, the International Longevity Summit will introduce scientific poster sessions and startup pitches, opening the stage to a new generation of researchers, entrepreneurs and innovators. Through an international Open Call, selected participants will have the opportunity to present research projects, scientific posters, short talks and startup initiatives to an audience of experts, investors, physicians and longevity enthusiasts. The goal is to make the Summit not only a place where established leaders discuss the future, but also a platform where the next generation of breakthroughs, companies and scientific careers can begin.

A distinguished group of prestigious Spanish and international institutions is supporting this historic event, organized by International Longevity Alliance (ILA) at the Royal National Academy of Medicine of Spain (RANME) , in collaboration with the Official College of Physicians of Madrid (ICOMEM) and Madrid Innovation . International supporters include European Wellness and Triple Helix Science at the Gold level, as well as Novogenia and Nesa World at the Silver level. The event is also endorsed by leading foundations and organizations, including HealthGevity Nation, Hevolution Foundation, Human Longevity Inc., HumanityPlus, Immortalis, KHL Foundation, Life Extension Foundation, Lifeboat Foundation, Longevity Escape Velocity Foundation, Millennium Project, XPRIZE Foundation , together with innovative companies such as Cenegenics , GERO , and OXANA . This year, the Summit will also welcome a new generation of startups working in healthtech, healthcare innovation and longevity, with the logistical support of CRRATE and StartUp Olé Salamanca .
The 2026 edition aims to further strengthen Madrid’s role as a bridge between Europe, Latin America, North America and the rapidly expanding global longevity economy.

bodyOriginal.alt: LSM 4

bodyOriginal.text: Two days of UNESCO history before exploring the future The Summit will begin even before the scientific program officially opens. On September 28 and 29, participants will be able to join two special pre-conference excursions to some of the most remarkable UNESCO World Heritage sites surrounding Madrid. The first day will travel south-east to Alcalá de Henares, Aranjuez and Toledo . The second will head north-west to Ávila, Segovia and El Escorial .

The contrast is intentional: participants will explore centuries of Spanish and European history before returning to Madrid to discuss technologies that may transform the future of human life itself. From ancient cathedrals and royal palaces to cellular rejuvenation, artificial intelligence and longevity escape velocity, the International Longevity Summit 2026 promises a journey through both humanity’s past and its possible future.

This summer, Spain has shown the world how to win on the football field. This autumn, Madrid will invite the world to explore how humanity might also win the greatest matches of all: the race against aging!
UNESCO World Heritage Tours: September 28–29, 2026
Free registration for the Madrid Longevity March

Organizer: International Longevity Alliance
Information and registration: www.LongevitySummit.Madrid
Videos: Teaser · UNESCO Tours · Full 12-minute Promo
General inquiries: info@longevitysummit.madrid

bodyOriginal.text: José Cordeiro, PhD, is an engineer from MIT and MBA from INSEAD. He is director of the International Longevity Alliance, vicechair of HumanityPlus, fellow of the World Academy of Art & Science, senior fellow of The Millennium Project, founder of the International Longevity Summit in Madrid, founding faculty of Singularity University in Silicon Valley, former Spanish candidate to the European EurParliament and coauthor of the international bestseller The Death of Death .

articles.titleOriginal: Calcium Mishandling Contributes to Muscle Loss
articles.summaryOriginal: Researchers have discovered and explained how calcium mishandling in muscle cells leads to long-term muscle weakness in older people. Calcium is not […]

bodyOriginal.text: Researchers have discovered and explained how calcium mishandling in muscle cells leads to long-term muscle weakness in older people .

Calcium is not just for bones Skeletal muscle cells use calcium ions to control how and when they contract. This activity is modulated by CaMKII, a protein kinase that also regulates muscle adaptations in response to exercise [1] and serves a great many unrelated functions throughout multiple other tissues.

In young tissues, this system works well, with exercise producing reactive oxygen species (ROS) that are used to stimulate muscle growth [1]. However, with aging, this falls apart in multiple ways: calcium ions leak out of where they are supposed to be [2], mitochondria and calcium become uncoupled [3], and, as has been well-known for decades, ROS and oxidative damage are no longer properly mitigated [4]. The authors hypothesized that CaMKII signaling is involved in this dysregulation.

Constant expression weakens muscles In their first experiment, the researchers examined the muscles of 3.7-month-old mice and compared them to those of 33-month-old mice; 33 months is exceptionally old for a mouse, and mice of that age were provided by the gerontologist Dr. Rafael deCabo. These elderly mice had significantly smaller muscles than the younger group, substantially more CaMKII in muscle tissue, and more evidence of CaMKII activity while at rest. However, the researchers noted that the biomarker they used to detect activity, pT287-CaMKII, is not entirely consistent in various muscle tissues and CaMKII can be modified in many other ways [5].

To determine the effects of constant CAMKII activity in muscle, this team developed a adeno-associated virus (AAV) that caused it to become active only in that tissue. This AAV had local effects, meaning that the researchers were able to inject it onto only one tibialis anterior muscle of each individual mouse; the identical muscle on the other side was injected with a simple fluorescent reporter protein with no significant effects. Interestingly, feedback mechanisms caused natural CAMKII to be suppressed in the muscles that were given this artificial CAMKII increase.

Within less than two months, this increase in constant CaMKII caused the targeted muscles to shrink and become pound-for-pound weaker than the unmodified muscles in the same mice; direct stimulation at multiple frequencies found that the targeted muscles were unable to exert nearly as much force. While it did not impact total mitochondrial number, it had significant negative effects on mitochondrial organization. A similar experiment with a different cohort of mice found that, after nine months, the loss of muscle mass became even more significant.

Some of this muscle loss was found to be driven by inflammation. Blocking the inflammatory signal NF-κB while activating CaMKII blunted some of the effects; the muscles in this group did not become pound-for-pound weaker, but they still lost mass.

Age-related gene expression changes Gene expression was also significantly impacted. While there were some differences, the impact of constant CaMKII expression was broadly similar to that of natural aging in muscle, and the researchers identified many biochemical pathways that are increased both by natural aging and by increased CaMKII. Most notably, iron-handling pathways were significantly disrupted by CaMKII.

The researchers also injected naturally aged mice with CN19o, which inhibits CaMKII; while individual genes were not significantly affected, the sum total of gene expression was found to move towards a more youthful phenotype. While it did not increase muscle size in 21-month-old mice, suppressing CaMKII in these mice increased their ability to contract.

The researchers hold that age-related constant CaMKII signaling is a significant contributor to sarcopenia. In youth, this signaling is beneficial, but in an aged environment, it is apparently doing more harm than good. However, the researchers did not experimentally validate why constant CaMKII activation has the mitochondrial effects it does, nor did they fully elucidate the connection between calcium and iron signaling. Further work will need to be done to determine if CaMKII is a useful target in people.

articles.titleOriginal: Whistles marks 50 years by casting 50 customers found through mysterious fly-posters across London
articles.summaryOriginal: Weirdo helped the British fashion brand swap the usual models for "open-minded" women aged 19 to 72, found via guerrilla posters, shot in a single day and backed by new positioning and a sig...

bodyOriginal.text: Weirdo helped the British fashion brand swap the usual models for "open-minded" women aged 19 to 72, found via guerrilla posters, shot in a single day and backed by new positioning and a signature colour called Lemonade.

Fashion is a beloved passion of mine. I've always loved dressing up. I have fond memories of Topshop and Tammy Girl in my teens, and of watching The Clothes Show every Sunday evening with my mam, while my dad disappeared upstairs to tinker on the computer.

Brands like Whistles came much later. It was always considered pricey and high-end compared to other high street stores, so we never shopped there. As soon as I started earning my own money, though, I saved every penny to get the latest cuts. I remember one pair of black trousers that I treated like a precious treasure for years, until they finally went to the charity shop, battered but well-loved.

My girlfriends share similar stories. We have emotional connections to the places we once worshipped every Saturday, returning home loaded down with shopping bags. For me, it was "going up Hanley Duck" on the No.20 bus to the Potteries shopping centre. And Whistles was one of the concessions in Debenhams. Most likely the first place I looked.

Fast forward to today, and I've not given it much thought in a long while. My go-to brands these days are a mix of Japanese menswear and eye-wateringly expensive garments from Studio Nicholson or Soeur. (I've been banned from Redchurch Street. Never let me go there. Seriously.) But hey, I justify the cost by saying it's what helps me feel good rather than reaching for Botox like so many women my age are (I just can't quite bring myself to do it, even though the pressure is real). Anyway, I digress.

Whistles, would you believe, turns 50 this year (gulp) and it wanted to mark the occasion. Instead of turning to models or going through its archives, it fly-posted much of London with cryptic posters asking for "open-minded women". There was no explanation or brand mention, just a call to say what open-mindedness means to you. Remarkably, more than 2,000 people replied.

bodyOriginal.alt: Man in orange shirt wearing headphones leans against doorframe in Whistles campaign poster displayed in London Underground station with passing train
Woman in black dress standing against brick wall on London Underground platform with Whistles advertisement displaying yellow "WHISTLES" text

bodyOriginal.text: The posters were the brainchild of Weirdo, the London creative agency founded in 2021 by former pro athlete Louis Persent, which has since built a reputation for putting real people at the centre of campaigns for the likes of Arsenal, Bumble, and Snapchat. Whistles and Weirdo whittled the replies down to 50 women, aged between 19 and 72, most of whom had never modelled before. They were then photographed in a single day wearing the latest Whistles collection, set against a plain white backdrop, and each was interviewed about her life for social and film content.

Six of those women front the launch, including a BAFTA-winning documentary filmmaker, a mother and an entrepreneur. Fashion photographer Alice Neale shot them, and Archi Shah filmed them, mostly using a camcorder. The result is a two-minute film that goes out today across out-of-home, social, digital and in-store. This isn't the glossy campaign you'd expect in The Bible (that's Vogue to anyone who doesn't know). More nostalgic and raw, taking me back to those beloved shopping days in Stoke.

Along with the campaign, Weirdo has also evolved the Whistles identity, now positioned as "Designed for an Open Mind". Ah, that makes sense. And there's a new signature citrus colour called Lemonade, plus an overall tone that's described as "sharp and light".

"We're leaving behind rigid top-down campaigns and moving towards projects and commissions," says Louis. "It's an open approach to brand-building that's allowed us to shoot 50 women in one day, commission a friend group to shoot a summer collection on a trip to Athens, and have a pipeline of future projects that will keep exploring what it means to be designed for an open mind."

Speaking of the Athens shoot, it was one of a year's worth of pilot projects where a real bunch of mates shot the summer collection on holiday. Nice to see Whistles not going down the AI route like other high street retailers might be. That authenticity will do them proud, no doubt. And give my fashion industry pals a sigh of relief.

bodyOriginal.alt: Woman in burgundy leather jacket with sheepskin collar and blue jeans crouching against a bright yellow wall

bodyOriginal.text: All this was certainly needed because I'd almost forgotten about Whistles. It had felt a little tired in recent years. And the quality had dropped. Other brands came along like Cos and Uniqlo, and we women moved on. We talk, I'm afraid, and the conversation always goes like "they used to be good... try this other shop instead" (Mumsnet is brilliant for that sort of advice).

Brand loyalty is a brutal game. I can't imagine the pressure to stay relevant and loved. And brands that lose their way can always make a comeback. Just look at Topshop. A change of hands or marketing strategy can be a good thing.

When I watched the campaign film, I got quite emotional listening to the stories. So many resonated. It frightens me to think of how long ago those teenage shopping trips were, so seeing Whistles honour women like us, and our life experiences, felt very honest. Like it's capturing a collective mood.
Whether it brings me back through their doors (or onto their website), the jury's out. But it's a clever reminder of something we once loved, and that it might be worth visiting again.

articles.titleOriginal: Mother Design gives psychic platform Keen a folk-art rebrand that takes on minimalist wellness
articles.summaryOriginal: The independent studio reframes "psychic guidance" for modern life, with stunning illustrations by María Jesús Contreras. When I saw the name Keen land in my inbox on Wednesday night, I imme...

bodyOriginal.text: The independent studio reframes "psychic guidance" for modern life, with stunning illustrations by María Jesús Contreras.

When I saw the name Keen land in my inbox on Wednesday night, I immediately thought of the dorky-turned-cool footwear brand I love so much. Alas, it wasn't. Instead of walking shoes and unconventional sandals, this Keen is known as a leading online marketplace that connects people with spiritual advisors. Good lord. There must be a lot of money in psychic services because they've just had a rebrand courtesy of Mother Design, part of the Mother family.

The brief was, quite simply, to help broaden the appeal of psychic services, presumably to cynics like me, and establish Keen as part of a normal routine. Hey, I'm open-minded. If it tells you what might be coming next year and makes you happy, I don't see the problem. My mother's side is said to have "the gift", and my Nana used to tell me some crazy stories. A good friend of mine, a Buddhist monk for many years who lived in Tibet, now lives in a 16th-century home near Wales and has told me stories of soldiers marching through his living room. I'm not entirely convinced of spirits or an afterlife, but I also know I don't know everything. Besides, with a brand this good-looking, I might just start believing. Though it turns out... crystal balls and messages from beyond aren't really what Keen is selling.

bodyOriginal.alt: Keen's rebranded logo on left showing a lighthouse with "KEEN" text, and on right a smartphone displaying the Ace of Cups tarot card from the new design system
Keen logo in white letters on a red background

bodyOriginal.text: Given the unusual subject, Mother Design did some research beyond the usual category and spotted a cultural shift: people are increasingly turning to things like AI and coaching platforms for daily guidance, but what they're really seeking is perspective and support that helps them become unstuck.

This informed the brand's strategic positioning, shifting psychic services from predicting the future to helping people gain clarity in their lives. Keen's network of spiritual advisors can help in ways AI and algorithms never can, so Mother Design leaned into this "human guidance" angle. They wanted to reposition Keen as a wellbeing brand but avoid the usual minimalist design that features too prominently in the category, supposedly to evoke calm. "Wellness has become surprisingly uniform," says Jo Tulej, creative director at Mother Design. "White space, muted palettes, rounded typography and gentle promises have become the category default. We wanted Keen to feel just as calm and approachable, but in a way that was richer, warmer and unmistakably its own."

bodyOriginal.alt: Keen platform interface displayed on multiple devices showing red background with folk-art botanical illustrations by María Jesús Contreras
Keen's rebranding exhibition space with illustrated panels depicting pastoral landscapes and city scenes flanking a central red wall with the Keen logo

bodyOriginal.text: So Mother Design went in the opposite direction from the usual chill vibes. The result? All-out hippy, psychedelic glory. I'm sorry, but I'm getting flashbacks of misspent youth here, rolling around Glastonbury's stone circle in a fuzzy mess. I like what I see. Nothing about this work is pared back. It's an identity that feels full of life and, well, very human.

Indeed, it's heartening to learn they worked with illustrator María Jesús Contreras to create an illustrated world that "captures the richness of life in all its wonder and familiarity". It draws on folk art mixed with cityscapes and countryside, spiritual symbolism, and everyday goings-on. It's like those days many years ago when you did something you shouldn't have and let loose with some paper and coloured pens. Together, it dreams up something lively for Keen. And instead of a collection of assets, it functions as a living thing, with scenes and symbols rolled out across Keen's website and communications.

bodyOriginal.alt: Vibrant folk-art illustration by María Jesús Contreras showing a busy landscape with people, buildings, nature and symbolic imagery representing clarity and human connection for the Keen rebrand
Orange line illustration of an atom with orbiting electrons on dark brown background, alongside a menu card and three geometric symbol designs on red background

bodyOriginal.text: Of course, there's always a risk of overwhelm. So Mother Design kept it easy on the eye with a few central themes. Circular forms and shifting viewpoints, for example, contrast nicely with the detailed backdrops by María Jesús Contreras.

The colour palette, apparently inspired by some of the earliest pigments used in human art, brings together grounding tones with warm neutrals and "optimistic accents". Typography pairs an expressive serif with a humanist sans serif – the idea being that it balances "ancient wisdom with contemporary accessibility".

Accompanying photography spotlights the real people behind the platform, adding that human touch. The verbal identity follows the same principle, with a warm, reassuring tone of voice. Online, Mother Design says it wanted to offer a "maximalist gasp in a world of minimalist wellness design". It's truly an identity you can't stop looking at.

bodyOriginal.alt: Red ochre and burnt umber pigment swatches displayed as oval colour samples with labels on a neutral background

bodyOriginal.text: "Our ambition wasn't simply to modernise Keen; it was to change how people think about psychic guidance," says Ariana Hellebuyck at Ingenio. "We wanted a brand that felt relevant to the way people approach wellbeing today while staying true to the spiritual expertise that has always set Keen apart. Mother Design struck that balance perfectly, creating an identity that feels more accessible and trustworthy without losing the authenticity of who we are."

Jo Tulej adds: "Broadening Keen's appeal was never about watering down what made it special. Instead, we built a brand world rooted in ancient wisdom, folk art and timeless symbols, then reinterpreted those influences through a contemporary digital experience. It feels familiar without being generic, spiritual without being intimidating, and modern without losing the authenticity that sits at the heart of Keen."

The new brand is now rolling out across Keen's website, app, and social channels. Which leaves me to say, whatever comes next for me, I hope it involves very good health and fortune. And possibly some tickets to Glastonbury, please.
